name: Delcy Rodríguez
role: Acting president of Venezuela (since January 2026); previously vice president (2018–2026), foreign minister, Constituent Assembly president, economy and oil minister
summary: A long-time chavista official who led Venezuela's foreign ministry, the 2017 Constituent Assembly and, from 2018, the vice presidency, and who became acting president after the US detained Nicolás Maduro in January 2026. Her record combines sovereigntist, anti-sanctions and anti-interference rhetoric with, in 2026, an oil-sector opening to private and foreign investors, cooperation with the United States, an amnesty law and a promise of elections. Her stated positions on social and cultural questions are largely unrecorded in the sources reviewed.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: At the 2026 UN General Assembly she criticized forced decarbonization projects as risking industrial collapse, employment and food security in oil-producing countries; she did not address government action on climate change as such.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: On 29 January 2026 she signed the reform of the Organic Hydrocarbons Law, 'the most significant reform to its hydrocarbons regime since the sector was nationalized in 1976' (HSF Kramer), letting private and foreign companies explore, produce and market oil directly, with royalties cut to as low as 20% (15% in some cases) to attract investment.

national-resource-control.rationale: The hydrocarbons law she signed in January 2026 keeps reserves state-owned but lets private and foreign firms run fields and sell crude, widens executive discretion over contracts, and adds independent arbitration clauses allowing disputes to be settled outside Venezuelan courts.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: At the 2026 UN General Assembly she called for respect for 'los derechos de la naturaleza' (rights of nature).

public-ownership.rationale: On 29 January 2026 she signed the overhaul of the Organic Hydrocarbons Law, which ends the rule that private oil companies must operate through joint ventures in which the state company PDVSA holds the majority: companies can now explore and produce under contracts and run fields at their own cost with 'less than a majority stake'. Reserves stay state-owned and PDVSA remains, so the shift is partial.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: On 28 September 2026, as acting president, she formally asked the National Assembly to reform the 2017 Constitutional Law against Hatred in order to decriminalise its offences ('avanzar en la despenalización de las conductas'); the reform bill she initiated keeps hate speech, war messages, harassment and discriminatory messages as infractions, defined as speech that directly and clearly promotes violence, discrimination or violent persecution on grounds including race, religion, gender and political affiliation, now punished by fines of 500 to 10,000 times the official exchange rate or community work instead of prison.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: At the 2017 UN Human Rights Council she called for a new international order limiting the financial powers she blamed for poverty and inequality.

state-directs-investment.rationale: In October 2026 she defended measures to direct bank credit toward productive and industrial sectors.

suppress-opposition.rationale: In January-February 2026, as acting president, she asked for and promulgated an amnesty law, unanimously approved on 19 February, covering anyone prosecuted or convicted for offences committed in the 27 years of chavismo, including those after the 2002 coup attempt and the protests after Maduro's 2024 re-election, so as to free hundreds of political prisoners; it excludes human-rights violations and those who promoted armed or force actions by foreign states against Venezuela.

notes:
Positions changed sharply after January 2026: she now cooperates with the US, thanks Trump, and promotes private and foreign oil investment, while still calling Maduro the legitimate president (NBC interview). Dollarization: rejected in 2021 and again in October 2026. Gaza: in 2023 she called Israel's offensive genocide, but no statement matches a current statement in the test. Essequibo: she asserts Venezuelan rights under the 1966 Geneva Agreement and asks Guyana to drop the ICJ case; no test statement fits cleanly, so it is left null. Her 2024 claim that opposition tally sheets were forged is a government position on a specific dispute and is not used for any statement. Unreachable: NPR amnesty article (timeout), El Colombiano (redirect loop), a mirror of a Sputnik piece on ties with China/Russia (connection refused), the later half of Wikipedia (no body text).

Later pass (claude-sonnet-5-5, 2026-11-14), brought to rules 7 and deepened: restrict-hate-speech is re-based on her 28 Sep 2026 reform initiative (the Supreme Court's ruling reproduces her letter and the bill). The CNN and NPR interviews (2015, 2017, 2019) in the local news corpus and her 2026 UN General Assembly speech (El Diario report) were read for further positions; they state none that settles a statement beyond the answers already recorded (aid as 'poisoned', Petrocaribe, sanctions, elections 'en igualdad de condiciones', justice reform, Essequibo under the 1966 Geneva Agreement). Added from agency and law-firm reports of the articles of her acts: the January 2026 hydrocarbons law (public-ownership, expand-fossil-fuels, national-resource-control re-sourced to acts) and the February 2026 amnesty law (suppress-opposition). Not done: the law texts themselves and the 2017 hate law as her act as Constituent Assembly president.
